thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — reserved GPU pool 'resv-prod-eu' at 100% utilization for enterprise tenants. Autoscaler attempting scale, failures detected. Queue depth rising for reserved queue.
ryan_oncall: I'm on it. pinging SRE. what's the customer impact?
ana_sre: oncall -> ana_sre. ETA 5m. seeing sustained enqueue rate ~220 req/s from reserved routes, tail latency climbing.
lee_runtime: adding logs — autoscaler reports create->terminate loops for instance group ig-resv-eu-1, messages: "GPU init timeout" then "instance not ready, deleting".
ryan_oncall: do we have a root cause yet? driver vs runtime mismatch?
ana_sre: suspecting recent driver rollout on those nodes. kube events show nodes cycle with taint "gpu-init-failed" then removed from pool. autoscaler not recognizing healthy replacements.
lee_runtime: paste of recent autoscaler error batch:
```
2026-03-15T03:14:02Z autoscaler: provisioning ig-resv-eu-1/instance-47
2026-03-15T03:14:49Z kubelet: GPU driver missing required module
2026-03-15T03:14:50Z autoscaler: instance-47 healthcheck failed -> terminate
2026-03-15T03:15:01Z autoscaler: rate-limit reached for create attempts
```
ryan_oncall: ok. that explains nodes not joining. can we scale to other regions or burst to shared pool?
ana_sre: reserved pool is pinned, but we can failover reserved tenants to dedicated-shared fallback policy (costly). need product/CS signoff for customer-impactful fallback.
jamie_csm: reporting to AuroraFinance (enterprise customer) now. hint: they are latency-sensitive SLAs. need to minimize migration impact.
lee_runtime: quick mitigation candidates:
- evict noisy tenant(s) on reserved pool to free GPUs
- temporarily increase reservation quota (if infra permits) and route new capacity to reserved pool
- route enterprise traffic to nearby dedicated-shared with throttling and model-downscale
- hotpatch node image to restore driver and let autoscaler succeed
ryan_oncall: who can do evictions quickly? we have evict-bot runbooks.
evict-bot: evict-bot here. I can evict long-running sessions older than 30m on reserved pool. need manual approval `:thumbsup:` from SRE lead.
nana_sre: approving evict-bot run for 30m threshold to free up 2 GPUs. running command: `evict-bot run --pool resv-prod-eu --age 30m --dry-run=false`
lee_runtime: executing safety checks. marking sequence in ops log.
nana_sre: kicked off. expecting ~2.2 GPUs freed in ~90s.
ryan_oncall: jamie, will that be enough for AuroraFinance to see immediate relief?
jamie_csm: it's a good short-term fix but they'll likely see a drop in processing capacity for a subset of jobs. tell them we plan failover if needed.
oliver_pm: tagging: need timeline and customer comms. please keep me in loop.
lee_runtime: evict-bot finished: 3 sessions evicted, freed 2.6 GPUs. autoscaler now attempts new instance spinup. next step: watch nodes join.
nana_sre: nodes still not joining. new instances fail GPU init with same driver error. so eviction didn't fix root cause.
ryan_oncall: so we have free capacity but GPUs are unhealthy on new instances. can we hotpatch node image?
lee_runtime: hotpatch strategy: deploy alternate kernel module from canary image `rv-node-img:v2.14-fixgpu` to a small subset of instances in the pool. requires infra approval and ~3m rollout.
nana_sre: suggestion: while patching, start controlled failover: route AuroraFinance to dedicated-shared eu-west fallback with throttling at 30% to preserve SLAs. jamie, need consent.
jamie_csm: AuroraFinance: approve failover to shared for up to 10 minutes if it reduces errors. They accepted under condition of close monitoring.
ryan_oncall: initiate failover. set route: `route set --customer aurorafinance --fallback dedicated-shared-eu --max-qps 0.3`
lee_runtime: command executed. traffic trimming in progress. watch queue depth.
nana_sre: monitoring: reserved queue depth decreased 45% within 60s. dedicated-shared O/P saw ~18% increase but within expected headroom.
ryan_oncall: proceed with hotpatch. coordinate with infra to avoid mass disruptions.
lee_runtime: starting hotpatch on 2 nodes: `node-update --image rv-node-img:v2.14-fixgpu --nodes node-203,node-204`
nana_sre: logs show driver module loads successfully on node-203, node-204 -> kubelet registers GPU resources.
lee_runtime: autoscaler detects 2 ready nodes, assigns workloads, reserved pool capacity now reports +2 GPUs available.
nana_sre: monitoring latency: p50 back to normal, p95 dropping. queue depth trending down.
ojr: (system message) :white_check_mark: Incident update recorded to #incidents-log.
ryan_oncall: great. next steps: 1) roll hotpatch to remaining nodes in pool overnight with maintained fallbacks, 2) root cause RCA: driver rollout gating failure, 3) add a probe in autoscaler to avoid rapid create/delete loops and implement backoff escalation alerts.
lee_runtime: adding autoscaler patch PR to prevent immediate reattempts after GPU-init timeout and to surface clearer alerts to oncall.
oliver_pm: schedule customer follow-up and postmortem comms with AuroraFinance. include migration timeline and mitigations.
jamie_csm: sending post-incident note to customer with summary and ETA for full restore of reserved SLA.
nana_sre: closing the pager for now — reserved pool stabilized and no ongoing errors. marking as mitigated, not resolved. I'll start a follow-up thread for RCA. :thumbsup:
ryan_oncall: thanks everyone. handing back to SRE for RCA. :coffee:
summary: Pager for reserved GPU pool saturation; autoscaler create/delete loop due to GPU driver init failures; evicted sessions for short-term relief, initiated customer failover to dedicated-shared, hotpatched node image to restore GPU init, capacity restored. Follow-ups: RCA, autoscaler backoff, gradual hotpatch rollout.
